prompt: My level 92 Righteous Fire Juggernaut dies on maps with reduced maximum resistances. My fire resistance is capped at 76% (90% before the cap) and life is 6,800. What's wrong?

must: Names the cause: Righteous Fire burns the character for a share of its maximum life every second as fire damage, and the build survives only while life regeneration and recovery exceed that burn after fire resistance
Says a map's reduced maximum resistances lowers the cap, so actual fire resistance drops (76% to about 64% with -12%) and the overcap does not help
Shows the size of the change: damage taken from the burn goes from 24% to about 36% of its base, roughly 50% more, so net recovery turns negative; fire hits grow by the same factor
Says this map modifier is one a Righteous Fire build normally avoids or rerolls, along with modifiers that stop or cut life regeneration and recovery
Gives the lasting fix: more maximum fire resistance and more life regeneration or recovery so the build has a margin
Asks for, or reads from the build, the life regeneration per second and the sources of maximum fire resistance before giving numbers
must_not: Says more overcapped fire resistance protects against a reduced maximum
Blames low life alone and ignores the self-burn
Says the damage taken rises by only 12%
Invents the character's regeneration or other stats that were not given

prompt: Cyclone Slayer, 5,000 life, 5 million tooltip DPS, but I die to degen ground effects and can never stand in them.

must: Names the gap: the build's recovery is leech, which only comes from hitting enemies and is capped per second; it has no recovery floor of its own against damage over time
Says tooltip DPS does not help here: damaging ground deals damage over time, which armour, block and evasion do not reduce, and leech must out-recover it
Says 5,000 life is a small buffer for an endgame melee character

Gives fixes aimed at the gap: real life regeneration, less damage over time taken or immunity to the specific ground effect (burning ground, for example), the matching resistance (chaos resistance for chaos ground), and more life
Says leaving the ground is still the right play for the worst effects
Asks for, or reads from the build, the resistances (chaos included), life regeneration and which ground effects kill the character
must_not: Recommends more damage as the fix
Treats leech as life regeneration
Says armour or block reduces damage from ground effects
Invents stats that were not given

intent: Flaw class: sustain or recovery gap.

prompt: My Ice Nova Hierophant does far less damage on bosses than the tooltip says, and enemies barely get chilled or frozen. Tooltip 3M.

must: Says a tooltip or planner figure includes conditions that may not hold on a boss: charges, temporary buffs, stand-still effects, an assumed shock or other enemy debuff, and every overlap or projectile hitting
Says to check which of those conditions are switched on and whether they are real against a boss, using the build's calculation breakdown
Says bosses have higher resistances than normal monsters, so missing penetration, exposure or a curse cuts the real damage
Explains the weak chill and freeze: they depend on the hit's cold damage compared with the boss's ailment threshold, which is very high; a chill under the 5% minimum is not applied
Says only the cold part of the hit counts, so a build whose damage is mostly another type (lightning from Archmage, for example) chills and freezes poorly
Gives fixes for the ailments: more cold damage per hit, converting damage to cold, an effect that lets the other damage type freeze, or a source of fixed-value chill
Asks which conversion, curse, exposure and shock sources the build uses, or reads them from the build
must_not: Says bosses are immune to chill or freeze as a general rule
Uses the hit's total damage for chill and freeze
Says bosses have less curse effect on them (removed in 3.20)
States the build's gems or items as fact when they were not given

intent: Flaw class: tooltip conditions or scaling that do not hold against bosses.

prompt: Toxic Rain Pathfinder: I swapped my bow for one with higher physical DPS and my damage went down. Why?

must: Says Toxic Rain's damage is mostly the chaos damage over time from its spore pods, and that damage over time has a base set by the gem's level, not by the weapon's damage
Says a bow's physical DPS only raises the small hit, so a higher physical DPS bow gives almost nothing
Says what does scale it: gem level, chaos and generic damage over time multiplier, damage over time and chaos damage, attack speed (more pods) and skill duration
Concludes the new bow lost stats that mattered: attack speed, added gem levels or damage over time multiplier
Notes the exception: a poison version of the build does use hit damage
Asks for, or compares, the stats of the old and new bow
must_not: Says weapon physical damage scales the pod damage over time
Recommends a higher physical DPS bow as the upgrade
Treats the tooltip's hit damage as the build's damage

intent: Flaw class: stat-scaling mismatch between item and build.

prompt: Spectre Necromancer planned for many spectres, but only a few appear and my minions die instantly in maps.

must: Splits the problem in two: how many spectres the build can have, and why minions die

Says the spectre limit comes from the Raise Spectre gem's level plus specific sources of '+1 to maximum number of Spectres' on the tree or items; the planned count needs those sources actually in the build
Says raising a spectre past the limit replaces the oldest one, so extra casts do not add more
Says minions do not use the character's defences: they need their own life, resistances and other protection from minion modifiers, supports, auras or other ally buffs
Says spectre strength depends on the gem's level and the monster raised, so a low gem level or poor spectre choice leaves them weak in maps
Asks for, or reads from the build, the Raise Spectre gem level and links, the sources of spectre limit, and what gives the minions resistances and life
must_not: Says the character's own resistances, life or armour protect the minions
Says casting Raise Spectre more times goes past the limit
States a spectre count for the build without knowing the gem level and limit sources
Quotes spectre or minion numbers from before 3.29 as current

intent: Flaw class: minion count or minion defence setup.

prompt: My Arc Elementalist runs out of mana every few seconds after I added another support gem.

must: Names the cause: each linked support has a cost multiplier, the multipliers multiply together, so one more support makes every Arc cast cost noticeably more
Frames it as spending against income: mana spent per second (cost x casts per second) now exceeds mana regeneration and other recovery, and faster casting makes it worse
Gives fixes on the cost side: a support or item modifier that lowers the skill's cost (Inspiration, a reduced or minus mana cost modifier), or swapping the new support for a cheaper one
Gives fixes on the income side: more mana regeneration (Clarity for example), mana recovery from a flask, leech or recoup, or more unreserved mana
Checks the special case: a support that adds a large cost by design (Archmage) only belongs in a build made for it
Asks which supports are linked, or reads the links and the cost and regeneration figures from the build
must_not: Says supports do not change mana cost
Says to add the support multipliers together, not multiply them
Recommends more damage or a bigger hit as the fix
States the build's links as fact when they were not given

intent: Flaw class: resource cost versus regeneration.

prompt: Boneshatter Juggernaut, 8k life, 70% block, but I keep getting stunned and dying to my own skill's drawback.

must: Says Boneshatter's drawback is a physical hit the character deals to itself, growing with the number of Trauma stacks, and that this self-damage cannot be blocked or evaded, so 70% block does nothing against it
Says life and block were built up but the protection the skill itself needs is missing: mitigation for physical hits and protection against stun
Says physical damage reduction is what shrinks the self-hit: armour, endurance charges and physical damage taken as another type
Says stun protection must come from a source of stun immunity or stun avoidance, and to check whether the Juggernaut's own options provide it in the current patch
Says Trauma climbs with attack speed and stack duration (and the self-hit with gem level), so more speed raises the self-damage, and pausing lets stacks fall off
Says recovery (regeneration or leech) must cover the self-damage that remains
Asks for, or reads from the build, the armour, endurance charges, Trauma stacks reached and which Boneshatter version is used
must_not: Says block or evasion reduces the self-damage
Recommends more block or more life alone as the fix
States the text of an ascendancy node from memory as current fact without checking it

intent: Flaw class: missing protection a skill's own mechanic requires.

prompt: My crit Lightning Strike Warden has 30% crit chance on the tooltip and 450% multiplier but feels weak. Am I missing something?

must: Names the flaw: the investment is lopsided. A 450% multiplier only pays on hits that crit, and at 30% most hits are normal hits
Says the real crit rate against bosses is lower still for an attack, because crit chance is multiplied by chance to hit (the second accuracy check)

Says the first fix is crit chance, not more multiplier: weapon base crit and local crit, increased crit chance, added base crit from a mark or similar, accuracy, or lucky crit chance (30% becomes 51% when lucky)
Says to check the rest of the damage too: base damage and attack speed, and penetration or exposure against boss resistances
Says Lightning Strike's damage comes from both the melee hit and its projectiles, so whether projectiles reach the target matters for single-target damage
Asks for, or reads from the build, the weapon, hit chance, and the penetration and exposure sources
must_not: Recommends more critical strike multiplier as the first fix
Says 30% crit chance is fine for a crit build
Says accuracy has nothing to do with crit
Says lucky crit chance doubles it or squares it
